summary: Eviatar Shulman works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1998–2008), where he later held posts in 2009 and as a Mandel postdoctoral fellow at the Scholion center (~2013–2016).

Eyal Aviv is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello, Parimal G. Patil, and Michael Puett, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Leiden University (~1925–1934). Succeeding Jean Philippe Vogel in 1939, he held a post at Leiden University from 1939 to 1972.

Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, A. W. Barber, Ronald Neufeldt, Eliezer Segal, Wayne McCready, Xiaojie Yang, and K. L. Dhammajoti. He taught Nirupam Chakma and Yong Hua Shi.

Fabienne Jagou specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the École des hautes études en sciences sociales (~1993–1999) and became a Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 2001.

Fabio Rambelli works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Mentored by Allan G. Grapard, William F. Powell, and others, he held positions at Sapporo University as Associate Professor (2001–2002) and Professor of Religion and Semiotics (~2000–2010).

Fabrizia Baldissera works in Indology. She studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" (1969–2004) and held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1990–2000) and the University of Florence (~2000).
Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He served as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-kuei Li was a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua University and the University of Michigan. He held posts at the University of Chicago, Yale University, the University of Washington (~1949–1969), and the University of Hawaii (~1969–1973).
Fausto Gherardo Fumi was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied under Giuseppe Bardelli at the Scuola Normale Superiore's Classe di Lettere e Filosofia between ~1858 and 1862.

Fazun was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery, Wuchang Buddhist Institute, and under Taixu. He founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and served as president (1956) and director (1980) of the Buddhist Academy of China.

Ferdinand Benary was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied under Franz Bopp from ~1827 to 1829 and became an extraordinary professor in the theological faculty at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1831.

Ferdinand Diederich Lessing was a scholar of sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He taught at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1925–1935) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1935–1952), teaching Alex Wayman and Helmut Hoffmann.

Ferdinand Justi was an Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1854–1856) and under Theodor Benfey (~1856–1859), later holding a post at the University of Marburg from ~1865 to 1907.

Ferdinand Sommer worked in linguistics and Indology. After studying at the University of Freiburg (~1894–1895), he held academic posts at Leipzig, Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1926–1945).

Ferdinand de Saussure studied linguistics and Indology at Leipzig, Berlin, and Geneva under Curtius, Brugmann, Oldenberg, and Zimmer. He served as Maître de Conférences at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1880–1891) and Professor at the University of Geneva (1891–1913).
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University under the doctoral supervision of Aleksandra Wenta.

Fernando Tola was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the National University of San Marcos. He held posts at the University of Buenos Aires (~1964–1985) and served as director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2017).

Filippo Marsili specializes in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied as a graduate student at the University of California, Berkeley, under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, and Arcangela Santoro, and holds a post at Saint Louis University.

Finnian M. M. Gerety is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. After receiving his doctorate from Harvard University in 2015, he held a postdoctoral fellowship at Yale (2017–2018) and a visiting faculty post at Brown University (attested 2020).
